faq.q: What is an AI Facebook ad from a product photo?
faq.a: A square still or a tall clip made from a product link or a photo you upload. A generated actor can hold the item and speak a script. That person is not a real customer.

faq.q: Can this lower my Facebook ad costs?
faq.a: We do not promise a lower cost-per-result. You can make another version, with another actor or line, without paying for another shoot. Credits are charged per file, and the amount shows first.

faq.q: Are these files allowed in Facebook ads?
faq.a: Follow the current ad rules for the country where the ad will run. If Ads Manager asks you to label AI content, do that there. We do not guarantee approval.

faq.q: Do people know the ad is AI-made?
faq.a: The file does not hide that a person in it is generated. If the placement asks you to label AI content, do that in Ads Manager when you publish.

faq.q: What does a Facebook clip cost?
faq.a: A clip costs 24, 40, 60 or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15 or 30 seconds, and that price shows before you start. A still is 24 credits. If a job fails, those credits return on their own.

faq.q: Where do the headline and the price go?
faq.a: Add the headline, the price and the button when you publish to Meta, or in Ads Manager after download. The clip can already carry a spoken script and on-screen captions.

faq.q: Does the file include sound, captions or music?
faq.a: Yes. A clip can include a voiceover, captions and a music track. Change them in the editor, then publish to Meta or download. The file has no watermark.

faq.q: How do I turn a product link into a Facebook ad?
faq.a: Paste the product page. We bring in the pictures and the description, draft a script, and you pick an actor and a voice. Then publish to Meta, or download the file.

faq.q: How should I compare two versions?
faq.a: Change one thing at a time, such as the actor or the opening, then use [how to test ad creatives](/guides/testing-ad-versions) before you scale the winner. A batch can make those versions from the same link.
